note: Round-8 additions: twenty-five recent English-language patent documents in CNS, NEUROLOGY, PSYCHIATRY, PAIN and ANAESTHESIA, priority dates 2011-2024, one or two per drug class. Same schema as pdf_corpus_round6_manifest.json. source_url is provenance, not a required fetch - the PDFs are committed under benchmarks/corpus/ with SHA256SUMS. EVERY FILE IN THIS ROUND IS A PAGE EXTRACT, not the whole publication: `pages_kept` records exactly which pages of the original were kept and `pages_original` how many there were. n_expected counts the distinct compounds this manifest catalogues (resolved + generic + unresolved rows); n_resolved counts those carrying a PubChem CID. est_structures is the total number of DEPICTIONS on the kept pages and is much larger; for most documents it is a flagged estimate, see pdf_manifest_round8.json `structures_drawn_is_estimate`. Every CID was resolved from something PRINTED IN THE DOCUMENT, or by structure search on the hand reading, and then CHECKED against the drawing.
retrieval_note: Both round-6 routes still work and both were used. (a) The EPO publication server, unauthenticated, for any granted EP: https://data.epo.org/publication-server/rest/v1.2/patents/EP<number>NW<kind>/document.pdf - B1 only, an A1 request returns HTTP 500. Confirmed working this session (EP3494109NWB1 returned 200, 483 KB). (b) A read-through proxy asked for HTML reaches Google Patents where plain curl gets 503: `curl -H 'X-Return-Format: html' https://r.jina.ai/https://patents.google.com/patent/<ID>/en`. NEW AND FASTER: the same proxy reaches https://patents.google.com/xhr/query, and the JSON it returns carries a `pdf` field holding the HASHED patentimages path for every hit - so a single search yields directly fetchable URLs and the per-patent page fetch can be skipped entirely. Every PDF in this round was fetched that way. Google rate-limits the proxy after roughly six queries in quick succession (an HTML page titled 'Sorry...'), so searches were spaced 16-20 s apart. PubChem PUG-REST also throttles under four concurrent agents: expect PUGREST.ServerBusy and back off 4-30 s. Long or paren-heavy SMILES in the URL PATH trigger an NCBI 'WWW Error 803'; POST the SMILES as form data to https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/smiles/property/... instead, which never failed.

rejected.what: Takeda, 'Method for producing heterocyclic compound' - the soticlestat process application
rejected.why_rejected: TWELVE pages and ZERO chemical structures. The whole route is written out as chemical NAMES in running prose and the only figures are four XRPD patterns. It is a perfectly good process document and completely useless for an OCSR benchmark. US11174272B2 was taken instead, which draws soticlestat in its example table.

rejected.what: Virginia Commonwealth University, 'Naltrexamine derivatives bearing 5-member heterocyclic ring systems as opioid receptor modulators'
rejected.why_rejected: 103 pages, structure-rich, and the right therapeutic area - but every specific compound is a 6-beta-naltrexamine amide, a five-stereocentre morphinan. A hand-built SMILES for the parent 6-beta-naltrexamine returned CID 0 on the first attempt, which means the scaffold cannot be entered without exactly the kind of hand transcription that a wrong reference would silently punish. Rejected on the two-independent-views rule, not on document quality. It is the strongest candidate for a later round IF someone pins the scaffold against a trusted 6-beta-naltrexamine record first.

rejected.what: Teva Czech Industries, 'Solid state forms of tavapadon and processes for preparation thereof'
rejected.why_rejected: The only tavapadon document with drawn structures that the search surfaced, and it is unfetchable from this server: it is an EP A1, and the EPO publication server serves B1 only (an A1 request returns HTTP 500), while Google Patents carries no `pdf` field for it. Tavapadon (Parkinson's, D1/D5 partial agonist) is therefore absent from the round.

rejected.what: istradefylline, ciprofol, atogepant, tolebrutinib, centanafadine, viloxazine, mirogabalin, zuranolone, ganaxolone, ulotaront
rejected.why_rejected: Ten further CNS drugs were searched, several with three different query formulations each. For each of them the only documents with drawn structures were non-English (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian) or were formulation/method-of-use patents that draw nothing. The round is therefore lighter on Parkinson's disease and ADHD than intended; Parkinson's is represented only by US9630955B2_opicapone.

rejected.what: 'process for the preparation of <drug>' as a Google Patents query
rejected.why_rejected: Recorded because it wasted an hour. For about half the drugs this phrasing causes the DRUG NAME to be dropped from the query entirely: cariprazine, brexpiprazole, opicapone, ozanimod, pitolisant and sugammadex all returned the SAME six irrelevant hits (an ergoline patent, a promethazine process, a clopidogrel impurity...) with totals in the thousands. The bare drug name plus one distinguishing chemical word, with language=ENGLISH&type=PATENT in the url parameter, works reliably.
